title: Checks for compound statements (multiple statements on the same line).
summary: According to PEP 8, "compound statements are generally discouraged". Ruff takes this rule from pycodestyle and made it stable in v0.0.245.

title: Checks for multiline statements on one line.
summary: According to PEP 8, including multi-clause statements on the same line is discouraged. Ruff takes this rule from pycodestyle and made it stable in v0.0.245.

title: Checks for statements that end with an unnecessary semicolon.
summary: A trailing semicolon is unnecessary and should be removed. Ruff takes this rule from pycodestyle and made it stable in v0.0.245.
message_templates: Statement ends with an unnecessary semicolon

title: Checks for comparisons to None which are not using the is operator.
summary: According to PEP 8, "Comparisons to singletons like None should always be done with is or is not, never the equality operators." Ruff takes this rule from pycodestyle and made it stable in v0.0.28.
message_templates: Comparison to `None` should be `cond is None`
Comparison to `None` should be `cond is not None`

title: Checks for equality comparisons to boolean literals.
summary: PEP 8 recommends against using the equality operators == and != to compare values to True or False. Ruff takes this rule from pycodestyle and made it stable in v0.0.28.
message_templates: Avoid equality comparisons to `True`; use `{}:` for truth checks
Avoid inequality comparisons to `True`; use `not {}:` for false checks
Avoid equality comparisons to `False`; use `not {}:` for false checks
Avoid inequality comparisons to `False`; use `{}:` for truth checks

title: Checks for membership tests using not {element} in {collection}.
summary: Testing membership with {element} not in {collection} is more readable. Ruff takes this rule from pycodestyle and made it stable in v0.0.28.
message_templates: Test for membership should be `not in`

title: Checks for identity comparisons using not {foo} is {bar}.
summary: According to PEP8, testing for an object's identity with is not is more readable. Ruff takes this rule from pycodestyle and made it stable in v0.0.28.
message_templates: Test for object identity should be `is not`

title: Checks for object type comparisons using == and other comparison operators.
summary: Unlike a direct type comparison, isinstance will also check if an object is an instance of a class or a subclass thereof. Ruff takes this rule from pycodestyle and made it stable in v0.0.39.
message_templates: Use `is` and `is not` for type comparisons, or `isinstance()` for isinstance checks

title: Checks for bare except catches in try-except statements.
summary: A bare except catches BaseException which includes KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit, Exception, and others. Catching BaseException can make it hard to interrupt the program (e.g., with Ctrl-C) and can disguise other problems. Ruff takes this rule from pycodestyle and made it stable in v0.0.36.

title: Checks for lambda expressions which are assigned to a variable.
summary: Per PEP 8, you should "Always use a def statement instead of an assignment statement that binds a lambda expression directly to an identifier." Ruff takes this rule from pycodestyle and made it stable in v0.0.28.
message_templates: Do not assign a `lambda` expression, use a `def`

title: Checks for the use of the characters 'l', 'O', or 'I' as variable names.
summary: In some fonts, these characters are indistinguishable from the numerals one and zero. When tempted to use 'l', use 'L' instead. Ruff takes this rule from pycodestyle and made it stable in v0.0.34.

title: Checks for the use of the characters 'l', 'O', or 'I' as class names.
summary: In some fonts, these characters are indistinguishable from the numerals one and zero. When tempted to use 'l', use 'L' instead. Ruff takes this rule from pycodestyle and made it stable in v0.0.35.

title: Checks for the use of the characters 'l', 'O', or 'I' as function names.
summary: In some fonts, these characters are indistinguishable from the numerals one and zero. When tempted to use 'l', use 'L' instead. Ruff takes this rule from pycodestyle and made it stable in v0.0.35.
